articleBody:
- [ ] Doorway width measurement of at least 34 to 36 inches — Ensures manual wheelchairs and walkers pass through without scraping trim or knuckles.
- [ ] Solid wood wall backing plan behind drywall — Provides required structural support for secure grab bars and fold-down shower seats.
- [ ] 60-inch clear turning diameter or T-turn zone — Verifies enough unobstructed floor space exists for someone using a mobility device to turn around safely.
- [ ] Curbless shower pan depth and drain assessment — Determines whether floor joists need alteration to achieve a flush, zero-barrier walk-in entry.
- [ ] Comfort-height toilet selection (17 to 19 inches) — Reduces knee and hip strain during sitting and standing transfers.
- [ ] Accessible vanity with open knee clearance — Permits seated grooming and wheelchair approach without bumping base cabinets.
- [ ] Slip-resistance ratings on wet-area floor tiles — Prevents dangerous slips when flooring is coated with water and soap residue.
- [ ] Handheld showerhead and thermostatic valve — Allows simple seated bathing and shields against sudden water temperature spikes.
- [ ] Lever-handle faucets and hardware — Enables easy one-handed operation for individuals with arthritis or reduced hand strength.

How to Use This Checklist
